requirement_title: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true
requirement_text:
# REQ-2234: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2234
Type: bug

## Requirement

The analyzer does not work if `SuppressSourceGeneration = true`. This has happened since version 3.1.1. It still worked in 3.1.0.

(The upstream issue contains no further text, repro or comments. Anything beyond this is derived.)

## Acceptance criteria

- With `SuppressSourceGeneration = true`, the MessagePack analyzer still reports its diagnostics (MsgPack0xx rules) for code that violates them. (derived)
- Behaviour with `SuppressSourceGeneration = true` matches version 3.1.0, where the analyzer worked. (derived)
- Behaviour with `SuppressSourceGeneration` unset or false does not change. (derived)
- Source generation itself stays suppressed when `SuppressSourceGeneration = true`. (derived)

## Notes from discussion

No comments on the issue.

hunches.claim: For an opted-out type whose members have Key attributes, the new early continue skips the later key-recording and duplicate-key checks. Two members with the same key therefore produce no MsgPack005, despite the requirement that analyzer diagnostics continue to work and the new README explicitly promising key-uniqueness validation. The same pattern exists in both changed member-processing loops.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.SuppressSourceGenerationAnalyzerReceiptTests.SuppressedType_ReportsDuplicateKeys. The test compiles a SuppressSourceGeneration=true type with two [Key(0)] members and asserts MsgPack005; on the changed code both members are skipped before duplicate detection, so the assertion exposes the missing diagnostic.

hunches.claim: The early continue also bypasses the remaining processing of every keyed member, including the later recursive collection of that member's type. Consequently an opted-out type with a [Key] member whose type violates the serializability contract no longer gets MsgPack003, contradicting both the acceptance criterion and the README's explicit statement that member types are still validated.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.SuppressSourceGenerationAnalyzerReceiptTests.SuppressedType_ReportsUnserializableMemberType. It uses a SuppressSourceGeneration=true type with a keyed member of an unannotated, non-serializable class and asserts MsgPack003; the changed control flow skips member-type collection and the assertion exposes the missing diagnostic.

hunches.claim: When source generation is suppressed, a member carrying an attribute derived from KeyAttribute is skipped before its member type is collected. Consequently, a referenced type that lacks [MessagePackObject] no longer receives MsgPack003 (and any later member-specific checks are likewise bypassed), contrary to the requirement that analyzer diagnostics continue to work with suppression enabled. The same early continue was added to both the field and property paths.

receipt_plan.detail: Run the generated DerivedKeySuppressionReceiptTests.DerivedKeyDoesNotSuppressMemberTypeDiagnostics test. With build_property.SuppressSourceGeneration=true, a [MessagePackObject] container has a [CustomKey] property whose type is not annotated; the generator run should contain MsgPack003, but the new continue at TypeCollector.cs:1083 prevents member-type collection so the assertion fails. The equivalent field case is skipped at line 921.

hunches.claim: With SuppressSourceGeneration=true, a member using a KeyAttribute-derived attribute is skipped before the member's MessagePackFormatter attribute is examined, so formatter-related analyzer diagnostics are silently lost for that member even though analyzers are supposed to remain active.

receipt_plan.detail: Add an analyzer test with SuppressSourceGeneration=true and a [MessagePackObject] type containing a member annotated with both a custom attribute derived from KeyAttribute and an invalid [MessagePackFormatter(...)] usage that normally produces a MsgPack formatter diagnostic. Assert the same diagnostic is reported with suppression true and false; the suppression=true case will fail because execution continues before the formatter check. Repeat for the corresponding field/property loop if applicable.

hunches.claim: MsgPack017 is incorrectly classified as AOT-only and suppressed for types using runtime serialization. Ledger entry [L6] defines it as warning that an init property initializer is replaced by the type's default during deserialization; that behavior remains relevant when the dynamic resolver is used, so this change loses an applicable analyzer warning.

receipt_plan.detail: Add an analyzer test for [MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)] with a keyed init property having an initializer, and mark the initializer/property with the expected MsgPack017 diagnostic. The current source-generation-only test expects no diagnostic, so the new expectation should fail against this change.

hunches.claim: The mixed-key test does not verify the new early exit: it expects only MsgPack005, which is also the outcome when the member is subsequently added to stringMembers, so deleting the property-path continue leaves the test green.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:1158 delete-statement: continue; -> removed; expected to survive because MixedKeyKindsAreReportedWithoutAnalyzerFailure observes only the already-reported MsgPack005 diagnostic and the remaining member processing produces no additional observable difference for that input.

hunches.claim: No test mixes key kinds on fields, leaving the new field-path early exit uncovered; the existing mixed-key case uses properties and therefore exercises only the second loop.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:1013 delete-statement: continue; -> removed; expected to survive because no test declares fields with mixed integer and string keys.

hunches.claim: The duplicate-key tests cover properties only, so the new guard preventing duplicate integer-key fields from throwing in intMembers.Add has no killing test.
